intro.penguins: This was the town commons, when I was small. Everybody grew a little and shared the rest. Then folks got busy, and the brambles didn't. Help me bring it back? The board by the gate says what we need, one step at a time.
intro.gangsters: This lot was a garden when I was a kid. Then the crews used it as a dump, and the city looked the other way. I want it back. Help me? The board by the gate has the plan, one step at a time.

letter.penguins: Dear neighbour, the old commons west of town has gone to brambles. I mean to bring it back, and I could use a strong pair of hands. Take the west road out of the plaza. Mornings, I'm there. - Hazel
letter.gangsters: Hey. There's a vacant lot on the west road out of town, full of junk the crews dumped. I'm turning it back into a garden. I could use help. Mornings, I'm there. - Hazel

desc.penguins: Brambles, boulders and fallen logs have swallowed the old commons. Clear every patch so there's room to dig.
desc.gangsters: Years of dumped tyres, drums and junk. Haul every pile out so there's room to grow.

done.penguins: Look at that. You can see the old furrows again. My gran planted potatoes right where you're standing.
done.gangsters: First time I've seen the ground here since I was a kid. Smells like dirt instead of oil. That's a start.

beat.penguins: I'll keep hauling. First time anybody ever thanked me for it.
beat.gangsters: I'll keep hauling. First honest sweat I've had in years. Feels alright.

desc.penguins: The old shed has no roof and one and a half walls. Timber, planks and nails, and Gideon says he'll lend a hammer.
desc.gangsters: The shed's been stripped for scrap twice. Timber, planks and nails, and nobody's taking this one.

done.penguins: A roof! Tools off the ground, compost bin round the side. Help yourself to the share crate: whatever we grow, a third is yours.
done.gangsters: Lock on the door, compost round the side. The share crate's yours: a third of everything we grow. That's the deal.

tonight.penguins: That's everything. Gideon and Sal start after supper with lanterns. Two nights' work: frame first, then the roof.
tonight.gangsters: That's the lot. Gideon and Sal start after dark with work lights. Two nights: frame, then roof and lock.

night.penguins: The crew worked by lantern light: the commons shed has a roof. Come and see.
night.gangsters: The crew worked under work lights: the garden shed has a roof and a lock. Come and see.

progress.penguins: Hazel's crew framed the commons shed by lantern light: posts up, half the walls on. One more night for the roof.
progress.gangsters: The crew framed the garden shed under work lights: posts up, half the walls on. One more night for the roof and the lock.

beat.penguins: Hinges oiled, door hung true. If it ever squeaks, it isn't my work.
beat.gangsters: That lock's mine. Nobody's stripping this shed again.

desc.penguins: Four raised beds so the soil drains and the rabbits have to work for it. Planks, stone for the footings, fibre for twine.
desc.gangsters: Four raised beds: the ground under the lot isn't fit to eat from yet. Planks, stone footings, fibre for twine.

done.penguins: Four beds, square and true. Finn's already arguing about who gets the sunny one.
done.gangsters: Four beds. Finn keeps calling them 'the plots', like it's a heist. Let him.

tonight.penguins: Planks, stone, twine: all here. Finn's bringing his cousins tonight. Four beds in two nights, you'll see.
tonight.gangsters: That's all of it. Finn's bringing his cousins tonight. Four beds in two nights.

night.penguins: Four raised beds went up at the commons overnight. Finn says he only argued twice.
night.gangsters: Four raised beds went up at the lot overnight. Finn says he only argued twice.

progress.penguins: Two of the four raised beds stand at the commons; Finn ran out of nails and patience. Two more tonight.
progress.gangsters: Two of four raised beds are up at the lot. Finn ran out of nails. Two more tonight.

beat.penguins: I've claimed the sunny one. Hazel says nobody claims anything. We'll see.
beat.gangsters: Bed number two's mine. The score of the century.

desc.penguins: Empty beds feed nobody. Two dozen seeds, at least three kinds: the volunteers plant whatever suits the season.
desc.gangsters: Empty beds feed nobody. Two dozen seeds, three kinds or more: the crew plants whatever suits the season.

done.penguins: Seeds are in! Wren wrote down a soup she makes from whatever comes up first. She says it's for you.
done.gangsters: Seeds are in. Wren's got a stew she makes from whatever comes up first. Here, it's yours now.

beat.penguins: Plant them shallow, water them often, and talk to them. Don't laugh, it works.
beat.gangsters: Shallow, water often, talk to them. Don't laugh. It works.

desc.penguins: Hauling water from the river is breaking everyone's backs. Stone for the wall, copper for the pump, rope for the bucket.
desc.gangsters: Hauling water from the hydrant is getting us looks. Stone for the wall, copper for the pump, rope for the bucket.

done.penguins: Clear, cold and ours. Benno says he'll water the beds every evening now. Take a drink, you've earned it.
done.gangsters: Clean water, no meter. Benno waters every evening now. Drink up, it's on the house.

tonight.penguins: Stone, copper, rope. Benno and Gideon start on the wall tonight. Three nights to dig it out, wall it and seat the pump.
tonight.gangsters: Stone, copper, rope. Benno and Gideon start tonight. Three nights: dig, wall, pump.

night.penguins: The commons well is rebuilt: new wall, new pump, cold water. Benno wants you to taste it.
night.gangsters: The lot's well is rebuilt: new wall, new pump, cold water. Benno wants you to taste it.

progress.penguins: The commons well is cleared out to the water and the first stone course is laid. Benno says two more nights.
progress.gangsters: The lot's well is dug back out to the water and the first course of stone is down. Benno says two more nights.

progress.penguins: The well wall is waist high and the pump tripod is up. One more night to seat the pump.
progress.gangsters: The well wall's waist high, pump tripod up. One more night to seat the pump.

beat.penguins: Taste that. Cold as the bottom of the river, and none of the fish.
beat.gangsters: Taste that. No meter, no bill, no rust.

desc.penguins: A row of fruit trees along the south lane: cherry, plum, orange, apple. Fruit for the seed, fertilizer and sap to get them going.
desc.gangsters: A row of fruit trees along the back fence. Fruit for the seed, fertilizer and sap to get them going.

done.penguins: Eight little trees! Rook says the blossom will bring the bees. I wrote down my cobbler for you: you'll want it come fall.
done.gangsters: Eight trees on a vacant lot. Rook says the bees will find them. My cobbler recipe, for you. Don't share it with the crews.

tonight.penguins: Rook wants the holes dug and soaked tonight and the trees in tomorrow night, while the ground's cool. Two nights.
tonight.gangsters: Rook digs and soaks the holes tonight, trees go in tomorrow night. Two nights.

night.penguins: Eight young fruit trees stand along the commons lane, staked and watered.
night.gangsters: Eight young fruit trees stand along the lot's back fence, staked and watered.

progress.penguins: Rook dug eight planting holes along the commons lane and soaked them. The trees go in tonight.
progress.gangsters: Rook dug eight holes along the back fence and soaked them. The trees go in tonight.

beat.penguins: Three summers and you'll be climbing these for cherries. Trees don't hurry.
beat.gangsters: Three summers and there'll be fruit on a vacant lot. Trees don't hurry.

desc.penguins: Glass for the panes, iron for the frame, planks for the benches. With cold frames in front, the commons grows through winter.
desc.gangsters: Glass, an iron frame, plank benches. With cold frames out front, the garden grows straight through winter.

done.penguins: Warm as a kitchen in there. Juniper wants to grow her herbs inside, and the cold frames will keep greens coming in the snow.
done.gangsters: Warm as the laundromat in there. Juniper's moving her herbs in, and the cold frames keep greens coming all winter.

tonight.penguins: Glass, iron, benches. This one's the big job: footings, the frame, then every pane. Give us four nights, and mind the mess.
tonight.gangsters: Glass, iron, benches. Biggest job yet: footings, frame, then the panes. Four nights. Mind the mess.

night.penguins: The greenhouse is up! Every pane in, the cold frames dug out front. Come and feel how warm it is.
night.gangsters: The greenhouse is up. Every pane in, cold frames out front. Come feel how warm it is.

progress.penguins: The greenhouse footings are poured and the sills are down. Nothing to see yet but string lines and mud.
progress.gangsters: Greenhouse footings poured, sills down. Nothing to see yet but string lines and mud.

progress.penguins: The greenhouse's iron frame stands: every rib up, not a pane in yet. Gideon is very proud of the welds.
progress.gangsters: The greenhouse frame is up: every rib, no panes yet. Gideon won't stop talking about the welds.

progress.penguins: Half the greenhouse panes are in. Juniper has already claimed a bench. One more night.
progress.gangsters: Half the greenhouse panes are in. Juniper's already claimed a bench. One more night.

beat.penguins: My herbs have never had it so good. Come winter, this is the warmest room in the valley.
beat.gangsters: My herbs have never had it so good. Warmer than my clinic in January.

desc.penguins: Stalls, bunting and a table full of everything we've grown. Bring produce for the opening day and the whole town will come.
desc.gangsters: Stalls, bunting, a table full of everything we grew. Bring produce for opening day and the whole block will come.

done.penguins: The whole town came. The WHOLE town. From now on it's a market on the 7th, 21st and 28th. The 14th is festival day, so we'll all be in town. This is for you, from all of us.
done.gangsters: The whole block showed up. Even the crews kept it civil. Market on the 7th, 21st and 28th now. The 14th is festival day: whole block's in town. This is from all of us.

penguins: Hazel's out at the old commons west of town every morning, pulling brambles on her own. Somebody ought to help her.
The old commons used to feed half the valley. Now it feeds the rabbits.
gangsters: Hazel's out at the vacant lot on the west road every morning, hauling junk on her own. Somebody should help.
That lot west of town was a garden once. Then the crews started dumping there.

penguins: You can see the old commons from the road again. Hazel says next is the shed.
I walked past the commons. Clean as a dinner plate. Was that you?
gangsters: The lot's clear! First time in years you can see the ground.
You cleared the lot? Huh. The crews won't like losing their dump.

penguins: The commons shed has a roof again. Hazel's talking about raised beds now.
Gideon lent his good hammer to the commons. He never lends anything.
gangsters: The garden shed's got a lock now. Gideon's lock. Nobody's breaking that.
Hazel says the lot needs raised beds. Ground's too rough to plant straight in.

penguins: Four raised beds at the commons! Now all it needs is seeds.
Finn says he's claimed the sunny bed at the commons. Hazel says nobody claims anything.
gangsters: Raised beds at the lot. Seeds next, Hazel says.
Finn calls the raised beds 'the score'. Hazel's given up correcting him.

penguins: There are sprouts at the commons! Real ones!
The commons beds are planted. Hazel's walking around like a proud aunt.
gangsters: Stuff's actually growing at the lot. In this town!
The kids water the lot beds after school. Nobody told them to.

penguins: The commons well works again. Best water in the valley, Benno says.
Benno waters the commons every evening now. He hums.
gangsters: The lot's got its own well. No meter, no bill.
Benno waters the garden every evening. Says it's the quietest hour of his day.

penguins: Fruit trees at the commons. In a few seasons there'll be pies for everybody.
Rook planted a beehive by the commons orchard. The bees found it in a day.
gangsters: They planted trees on the lot. Trees! On a lot!
Rook says the bees found the lot orchard in a day. Bees know a good thing.

penguins: A greenhouse at the commons. Greens in winter, imagine that.
Juniper grows her herbs in the commons greenhouse now.
gangsters: A greenhouse on the lot. Winter greens, no imports.
Juniper's herbs live in the lot greenhouse now. Warmer than her clinic.

penguins: Market day at the commons is the best day of the week.
Posy sells her bread at the commons market now. Sells out by noon.
Did you see the commons on market day? The whole town was there.
gangsters: Market day at the lot garden. Best day of the week.
Posy sells out at the lot market by noon.
The whole block turns out for the lot market. Even the crews behave.

penguins: My back's not what it was. The commons won't clear itself, but it won't mind a second pair of hands.
Every town needs a place where anyone can grow something. Ours got lost under the brambles.
gangsters: I'm not waiting for the city to fix that lot. Nobody's waiting for the city anymore.
A garden's the one thing the crews can't shake down. You can't fence a tomato.

penguins: Come by the commons and check the beds. If something's ripe, pick it: it all goes in the stand.
The share crate's for you. Don't be shy about it.
gangsters: Something's always ripe at the lot. Pick it, it all goes in the stand.
Your share's in the crate by the shed. Take it.

penguins: I help Hazel at the commons in the mornings. Hauling things is the one thing I'm good at.
Nobody asks questions at a garden. I like that.
gangsters: I haul for Hazel at the lot mornings. Honest work. Weird feeling.
The lot's the only place in town nobody asks who I used to be.

penguins: I fixed the shed hinges at the commons. They'll outlast all of us.
If a commons tool breaks, bring it to me. No charge. Don't tell anyone.
gangsters: I put a lock on that garden shed. My lock. Let them try.
Garden tools, I fix free. Don't spread it around.

penguins: Beans and fish: the only two things worth growing. The commons only has room for one.
I tend the second bed at the commons after lunch. Fish don't bite at one o'clock anyway.
gangsters: I work the second bed at the lot after lunch. Fish don't bite at one anyway.
Planting's like fishing. You wait, then everything happens at once.

penguins: The commons soil is good. Old. It remembers being a garden.
I grow feverfew in the corner of the commons beds. Don't pick it, it's not a salad.
gangsters: The lot soil came back faster than I thought. Dirt's forgiving.
There's feverfew in the corner bed at the lot. It's medicine, not lunch.

penguins: I water the commons every evening. The horses can spare me an hour.
That well's deeper than it looks. Cold all summer.
gangsters: I water the lot every evening. Best hour of my day.
That well's cold even at the height of summer. Don't tell the President.

penguins: The commons orchard needs a few years. Trees don't hurry for anyone.
I watch the commons trees mornings. Deer love a young plum.
gangsters: I keep an eye on the lot trees mornings. Rats love a young plum.
Trees on a vacant lot. Funny old world.

penguins: I moved my herbs into the commons greenhouse. They've never looked better.
Fresh greens in winter keep me less busy. That's the whole point.
gangsters: My herbs live in the lot greenhouse now. Better than my windowsill.
Winter greens keep people out of my clinic. Best medicine there is.

penguins: I bake with commons flour and commons berries now. It tastes like home.
Market day, I sell out by noon. Come early!
gangsters: Everything I bake for market day is from the lot. People can taste it.
Market day, I sell out by noon. Come early, boss.

penguins: The commons is the best thing to happen to this town's budget in years. It costs nothing.
I've put the commons in the town records. Officially, it's a park now.
gangsters: The lot garden is officially a park now. I filed it myself. Let the developers argue with a park.
Civic pride, at last. And at no cost to the treasury.

penguins: Weeds don't take days off, so neither do I.
Look at these roots! Healthy as anything.
Mind the edges, the seedlings are shy.
gangsters: Weeds don't take days off. Neither do I.
Look at these roots. Ground was junk a season ago.
Mind the edges. Took us a month to get these going.

penguins: One more load and I'll sit down. Probably.
Heavy, but good heavy.
Everything here gets carried twice. Once in, once out as dinner.
gangsters: One more load, then I sit. Probably.
Heavy, but honest heavy.
Everything here gets carried twice. Once in as junk, once out as dinner.

penguins: Hinges, handles, the odd broken rake. Somebody has to.
Tools last forever if you clean them. Nobody cleans them.
gangsters: Hinges, handles, the odd bent rake. Somebody has to.
Tools come back clean or they don't come back. Shed rule.

penguins: Fresh today! Well, fresh-ish.
Prices are low because the soil works for free.
Take a look, everything's from the beds behind me.
gangsters: Fresh today. Grown fifty steps from here.
Prices are low because the soil doesn't pay rent.
Take a look. Everything's from the beds behind me.

penguins: Lunch tastes better outside. That's science.
Sit down a minute. The beds will still be there.
gangsters: Lunch tastes better on a lot you cleared yourself.
Sit a minute. The beds aren't going anywhere.

penguins: The board says what's next. Read it, then help me make it happen.
I like to see the plan with my own eyes.
gangsters: The board says what's next. Read it, then help me make it happen.
Plans on paper, pinned where everyone can see. No secrets on this lot.

penguins: I come here to think. And to watch the bees.
Best bench in the valley. Don't tell the park.
gangsters: I come here to think. Nobody looks for you on a garden bench.
Best seat on the block. Quiet, and you can see who's coming.

penguins: Rain's doing the watering for us. I'm just keeping the tools dry.
Nothing grows faster than a garden in the rain. Except mud.
We'll wait it out under here. The beds don't mind a bit.
gangsters: Rain does the watering. I'm keeping the tools dry.
Wet day. The beds love it, my boots don't.
We wait it out under here. Dirt doesn't care.

penguins: Winter's for mending and planning. And the greenhouse, thank goodness.
Cold hands, warm compost.
gangsters: Winter's for fixing things and planning. And the greenhouse.
Cold hands, warm compost. That's the trade.

penguins: Market day! Have you tried Posy's bread yet?
Half the valley's here. Isn't it wonderful?
Sell at the stand today, folks pay well.
gangsters: Market day. Whole block's out.
Try the bread before it's gone.
Sell at the stand today. People pay good.

ask_text.penguins: Market's going strong, but the soup kitchen runs short this time of year. If you can spare it, bring {need}. The whole commons will thank you.
ask_text.gangsters: Market's doing fine, but the block's short this time of year. Bring {need} if you can spare it. Everybody eats.

penguins: You can tell a lot about a person by how they hold a hoe. You hold it like you mean it.
gangsters: You hold a hoe like you mean it. Good.

penguins: Strong back, quiet mouth. That's what Hazel wanted, that's what she got.
gangsters: Strong back, quiet mouth. That's the job.

penguins: This rake's older than you. Still pulls true.
gangsters: Rake's older than you. Still pulls true.

penguins: Worms are worms. Garden worms, fishing worms. I don't judge.
gangsters: Worms are worms. I don't judge where they came from.

penguins: The feverfew's coming up nicely. Don't eat it.
gangsters: Feverfew's coming up. Still not lunch.

penguins: Mum says I've got green fingers. They're just muddy.
gangsters: Mum says I've got green fingers. They're just dirty.

penguins: I found a worm this long! Then it left.
gangsters: I found a worm this long! Then it left.

penguins: I'm guarding the trees. From what? Everything.
gangsters: I'm guarding the trees. From who? Everybody.

penguins: Two buckets a bed. The horses could do it faster, but they won't.
gangsters: Two buckets a bed. Quietest hour in town.

penguins: Bees found the blossom before I did.
gangsters: Bees found the blossom before I did. Good scouts.

penguins: Mint wants the whole greenhouse. Mint can't have it.
gangsters: Mint wants the whole greenhouse. Mint doesn't get it.

penguins: Compost is just old dinner having a nap.
gangsters: Compost is old dinner taking a nap.

penguins: I'm sketching the beds. The light's perfect on the kale.
gangsters: Sketching the beds. The kale's got good bones.

penguins: Did you know the old commons had forty-one kinds of apple? I'm writing it down.
gangsters: This lot was an orchard before the city had streetlights. I checked the records.

penguins: Officially a park. Unofficially the best thing I've signed.
gangsters: Officially a park now. Best thing I ever signed.

penguins: Morning!
Hello there!
Nice day for it!
Oh, hi!
gangsters: Hey.
'Sup.
Look who it is.
Hey, you.

penguins: Pull, don't snap...
These are coming on!
Ooh, a big one.
gangsters: Pull, don't snap...
These are coming on.
Ooh, a fat one.

penguins: Heave!
Mind your toes!
Last load. Ish.
gangsters: Heave!
Watch your toes!
Last load. Maybe.

penguins: Tap, tap...
There we go.
Who bent this?
gangsters: Tap, tap...
There we go.
Who bent this?

penguins: Fresh greens!
Two for one!
Try a slice!
gangsters: Fresh greens!
Two for one!
Get it while it's hot!

penguins: Mmm!
Pass the bread?
Lovely.
gangsters: Mmm.
Pass the bread?
Not bad.

penguins: Ahh.
Listen to the bees.
gangsters: Ahh.
Quiet, huh?

penguins: Next on the list...
Hmm, hmm.
gangsters: Next on the list...
Hmm.

penguins: What a downpour!
Free water!
Brr!
gangsters: What a downpour!
Free water.
Brr.

ask.penguins: Weeds keep coming up round the bed frames faster than I can pull them. Grab a few for me?
ask.gangsters: Weeds keep coming up round the bed frames. Pull a few for me?

go.penguins: Pull the weeds round the beds (marked with leaves).
go.gangsters: Pull the weeds round the beds.

done.penguins: Lovely and tidy. Here, take some of what we grew.
done.gangsters: Clean as a whistle. Here, take a cut of the harvest.

ask.penguins: There's a stack of crates that needs carrying to the %s. Give me a hand?
ask.gangsters: Stack of crates needs hauling to the %s. Got a minute?

go.penguins: Carry the crates to the %s, one at a time.
go.gangsters: Haul the crates to the %s, one at a time.

done.penguins: That's the lot. Strong arms! Here, for your trouble.
done.gangsters: That's the lot. Here, for your trouble.

ask.penguins: The beds are thirsty and the river's a long walk. Water a few for me? Grab your can.
ask.gangsters: Beds are dry and the hydrant's a hike. Water a few? Bring your can.

go.penguins: Water the dry beds near %s with your can.

done.penguins: Listen to them drink! Thank you. Here, take some of this.
done.gangsters: They'll be fat by market day. Here, take some of this.
